clinical_features.symptoms:
Clinical features: 
agitation, delusions, paranoia, tachycardia, 
hypertension, hyperthermia, mydriasis, 
hyperreflexia, seizures 
*Investigations: 
ECG for tachydysrhythmias, monitor for 
rhabdomyolysis 
*Specific management: 
•
Benzodiazepines for agitation 
•
Supportive care 
•
Avoid Beta-blockers – unopposed alpha agonism 
 
 
 
CHOLINERGIC 
TOXIDROMES 
 
 
 
SEDATIVE-HYPNOTIC 
 
*Common agents: 
Organophosphates, Carbamates, Physostigmine, 
mushroom toxins 
*Clinical features: 
Salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhoea, 
vomiting, sweating, miosis, fasciculations, 
brady/tachycardia, confusion, seizures 
*Investigations: 
As per toxicology protocols, 
pseudocholinesterase levels if diagnosis in doubt 
*Specific management: 
Atropine boluses/infusion 
SEE ACETYLCHOLINESTERASE INHIBITOR OVERDOSE PROTOCOL FOR FURTHER DETAILS 
* Common agents: 
Opioids, benzodiazepines, barbiturates, Nyaope & 
other opioid based illicit substances 
* Clinical features: 
sedation, coma, respiratory and cardiovascular 
depression, miosis/mydriasis 
* Investigations: 
Clinical dx, consider urine drugs of abuse screen 
* Specific management: 
• Opioids: Consider Naloxone 0.04 – 2 mg IV boluses 
• Benzos: Avoid Flumazenil – can precipitate withdrawal/seizures 
MAINSTAY OF TREATMENT FOR ALL SEDATIVE-HYPNOTICS IS VENTILATORY AND 
CARDIOVASCULAR SUPPORT 
 
 
 
 
 
ANTICHOLINERGIC 
* Common agents: 
Antihistamines, antiparkinsonians, 
atropine, antispasmodics, plant 
toxins – Devil’s trumpet, Jimson 
weed, Nightshade 
* Clinical features: 
Delirium, tachycardia, dry/flushed 
skin, dilated pupils, hyperthermia, 
myoclonus, urinary retention, 
seizures, decreased bowel sounds 
* Investigations: 
ECG – monitor for 
tachydysrhythmias 
* Specific management: 
•
Benzodiazepines for agitation 
•
Consider activated charcoal, 
•
Consider physostigmine (expert consultation)
